intro: Sentence-final の is the nominaliser の closing the sentence: it presents everything before it as 'the situation' or 'the explanation'. With a rising voice it asks the listener to explain the situation (どうしたの？); with a falling voice it gives the explanation (頭が痛いの). It is the casual counterpart of んですか and んです.

skills.rule: In casual speech, end with a rising の to ask about the situation, and with a falling の to explain it.
skills.explain:
Rising の is the normal, friendly way to ask a question in casual speech: どこ行くの？ 何してるの？ (A bare rising 行く？ also works; の adds 'what's going on?'.) It asks about the situation in front of you, often with curiosity or concern: どうしたの？ 'what's wrong?'; 本当に行かないの？ 'you're really not going?'. Falling の explains or insists softly, 'the thing is...': 今日は行けないの。熱があるの. This falling use sounds feminine or childlike; men tend to say んだ.

Nouns and な-adjectives take な before の: 学生なの？, 好きなの. Verbs and い-adjectives attach directly: 行くの, 高いの. 学生だの is wrong.

The polite equivalent is んですか / んです: どこに行くんですか. Do not use bare の to a teacher, a boss or a stranger. A firm, falling の from a parent can also be an order: 早く寝るの！ 'bed, now!'.

examples.jp: 何[なに]を食[た]べてる{の}？
田中[たなか]さんは学生[がくせい]な{の}？
今日[きょう]は行[い]けない{の}。熱[ねつ]がある{の}。
examples.en: I can't go today. I've got a fever, you see.

contrast.note: In casual speech, bare か sounds rough or interrogating (何を食べているか？), and 行くか？ often means 'shall we go?'. の is the neutral casual question. In polite speech か is normal: どこに行きますか.
Falling の explains, よ informs: 頭が痛いの, 'it's that my head hurts'; 頭が痛いよ, 'my head hurts, I'm telling you'. They combine: 痛いのよ.
ね asks for agreement about something shared: 寒いね. の asks for or gives an explanation: 寒いの？ 'are you cold?' (why are you shivering?).

mistakes.bad: 田中[たなか]さんは学生[がくせい]だ{の}？
mistakes.good: 田中[たなか]さんは学生[がくせい]な{の}？
mistakes.note: Nouns and な-adjectives take な, not だ, before の.

mistakes.bad: 先生[せんせい]、どこに行[い]く{の}？
mistakes.good: 先生[せんせい]、どこに行[い]くんです{か}。
mistakes.note: Bare の is casual. To a teacher, use the polite form んですか.

mistakes.bad: （友達[ともだち]に）何[なに]を食[た]べている{か}？
mistakes.good: （友達[ともだち]に）何[なに]を食[た]べてる{の}？
mistakes.note: To a friend, a casual question ends in の; bare か sounds like an interrogation.

skills.tip: Casual question, rising voice? の. Same question to your boss? んですか.
